this paper presents two compact patch antenna structures for outdoor RF energy harvesting, with one design having a slotted ground plane for size reduction, and both achieving a good impedance match to a 50-ohm load.
the slotted ground plane FSPA has a better performance, in terms of size and bandwidth, than the FSPA with small ground plane.

the FSPA design is suitable for outdoor RF energy harvesting applications, and that a slotted ground plane can be used for further size reduction.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the FSPA structure with a slotted ground plane is an attractive antenna design for outdoor RF energy harvesting applications.
the FSPA design with slotted ground can achieve a comparable impedance bandwidth with an overall size reduced by 29% compared to the FSPA design.
the slotted ground plane design can provide an alternative approach to reducing the size of the FSPA antenna for outdoor RF energy harvesting.
